name: Vashti
role: Queen of Persia who refused the king
whenBasis: The third year of Xerxes (Esther 1:3), taking him as Xerxes I, as Carey Moore identifies him, who reigned from 486 BC.
summary: Queen of Xerxes, who gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace while the king feasted. On the seventh day, merry with wine, the king sent seven eunuchs to bring her before him wearing her royal crown to display her beauty. She refused. On Memucan's advice the king decreed that she should never again enter his presence and that her position be given to someone better, and sent letters to every province that every man should be master of his own household.
body: The text gives no reason for her refusal. Her fall opens the way for Esther.

moments.text: Every man master of his household
Esther made queen in her place

later.text: The Talmud says she was ordered to appear wearing only the crown, and that she was a granddaughter of Nebuchadnezzar.
traditions: the Talmud and later rabbinic midrash

later.text: Herodotus names Xerxes' queen as Amestris. George Rawlinson identifies Vashti with her, the two names being different renderings of the Persian or Vashti a title, and takes her deposition to have been temporary; Carey Moore finds no Vashti or Esther in the Greek historians.

sources.title: Esther (Ellicott's Commentary for English Readers), on 1:9
sources.author: ed. C. J. Ellicott
sources.note: 'we may with Canon Rawlinson say that Vashti is Amestris (the two names being different reproductions of the Persian, or Vashti being a sort of title) and that the deposition was a temporary one'

traditions: Vashti is Amestris: George Rawlinson, as Ellicott's commentary reports him
no match in the Greek sources: Carey A. Moore
